title: Efficient and Scalable Neural-Symbolic Search for Complex Query Answering over Incomplete Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Complex Query Answering aims to answer first-order logical queries from incomplete knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: Existing neural-symbolic methods face quadratic data-complexity scaling, NP-hard query complexity for cyclic queries, and resulting scalability difficulties.

contributions.claim: An efficient and scalable symbolic search method with constraint strategies and a local search algorithm.
Constraint strategies reduce the variable search domain, while local search approximately solves NP-hard cyclic queries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On various CQA benchmarks, the method achieves 97% relative MRR for tree-form queries with a 10× speedup using 10% of the search space.
The method demonstrates robust performance on complex cyclic queries and large-scale knowledge graphs.
The authors report that code is provided in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work concerns answering first-order logical queries over incomplete knowledge graphs.
Existing neural-symbolic methods encounter data- and query-complexity bottlenecks that impede scaling.
The proposed method combines search-domain constraints with local search for cyclic queries.
The authors report strong efficiency results for tree-form queries and robust performance on cyclic queries and large-scale graphs.
Code is reported as publicly provided.

source_observation.claim: Reducing the variable search domain is associated with the reported 10× speedup using 10% of the search space for tree-form queries.

interpretation.claim: Search-space reduction may be a practical route to improving CQA efficiency.

application.claim: For large or incomplete knowledge-graph query systems, prioritize mechanisms that constrain candidate variable assignments before expensive search.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the reported efficiency applies equally to all query forms or knowledge-graph settings.

unknowns: Benchmark identities, dataset sizes, baselines, and evaluation protocols are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results for cyclic queries or large-scale knowledge graphs.
The constraint strategies and local search algorithm are not described in implementation detail.
